question:
RECOMMEND: APPROVE — advance to spec, on the Round A scope, now measured rather than proposed.

Why: your question is answered. On a like-for-like basis — same payer, same 14 categories — you did not double your spending, you cut it 44%. The apparent doubling is entirely coverage: eleven cost categories entering your record between 2023 and 2025, plus a second payer entering it. Mortgage alone is the single largest term, and it is now sized: adding your 2023 mortgage payments closes 35.2% of the gap by itself.

DECISION EFFECT: approve advances 060 to spec, which writes the deliverable — the honest comparison, the labelled reasons, and a first glide path — as a private report. Reject holds it at ideation.

ONE THING THAT IS NOT YET DECIDED AND SPEC OWES YOU: how the like-for-like comparison gets computed. Reports has a payer filter but no category filter, so restricting 2025 to your 14 shared categories needs either hand-summing off the Annual breakdown or a small read-only script. That is a delivery-mechanism choice, not a finding, and spec should propose it rather than assume it.

ONE CANDIDATE THE DATA CANNOT SETTLE, AND IT IS YOURS: inside the 11 new categories, Babies is the second-largest term at 30.3% of the gap — nearly as large as Mortgage. Unlike Mortgage, Insurance, Rent, Tax and Tenant, which are plainly costs you were already paying and not recording, Babies is not self-evidently a coverage effect: Tuition is a separate category present in all three years, so Babies is a genuinely new bucket. Whether those costs existed under some other heading in 2023 is something only you can say, and the report's honesty depends on it.

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS ENTITY'S OWN EARLIER DRAFTS, SO THE RECORD IS ACCURATE: it twice said no app total could be compared against your NT$1.2M target. That is now known false for 2025 specifically — your own planning workbook copies the app's annual total into a column headed "Life spend from earnings", so by your own construction the app total for 2025 IS your life-spend measure. And the glide-path reference has changed: not the archive workbook's old projection table, but your current Coast FIRE Annual tab, which you are already using and both credentials can read.

DELIVERY CONSTRAINT UNCHANGED: this repository is public and every figure above is a ratio or a share for that reason. The report itself is delivered privately; the entity records only its location.

artifacts.summary:
SEED OUTCOME, sharpened twice: answer why recorded spending appears to have roughly doubled from 2023-2024 to 2025, and propose a realistic path back down. Cycle 1 planned an 18-year archive analysis; the captain's own question narrowed it to a three-year comparison the app can already serve; this cycle's measurement narrowed it further, from a comparison to an answer.

WHAT THE APP CAN ANSWER TODAY: 2023 (895 rows, all 12 months, ijac only), 2024 (775 rows, ends 2024-11-08, ijac only), 2025 (1,404 source rows, ijac and wei). Reports > Annual gives, per year, total, per-category breakdown, per-payer breakdown, monthly trend and an AI insight, for any reachable year — 2023 through 2025 are all reachable now via entity 061's import. The payer filter works correctly; there is no category filter.

THREE TRAPS, ALL RESOLVED THIS CYCLE RATHER THAN LEFT AS CAVEATS:

TRAP 1 — PAYER ASYMMETRY. 2025 counts two people; 2023-2024 count one, by the captain's own ruling in 061 (the source workbook had no payer column because it only ever had one payer). Controllable via the Reports payer filter.

TRAP 2 — 2024's TRUNCATION. Record ends 2024-11-08, workbook's own December total and day sum both zero — the fortnight was never entered, nothing recovers it. Short by 53 days. Usable as monthly shape, not as an annual total.

TRAP 3 — CATEGORY COVERAGE, MEASURED THIS CYCLE. 2023 and 2024 each use 14 of the app's 25 categories; 2025 uses all 25. Eleven categories carry rows in 2025 and zero in both earlier years (Transportation, Digital, Babies, Gifts, Entertainment, Shopping, Rent, Mortgage, Insurance, Tax, Tenant), and not one category runs the other way — the signature of a coverage change, not a spending change. Mortgage: 12 rows in 2025 (one a month), zero before. Two more near-absent rather than absent: Sports 6/2 rows to 59; Donate 1/3 to 48.

TRAP 3 REVERSAL, CORRECTING THIS ENTITY'S OWN EARLIER TWO DRAFTS: both stated no app total is comparable to NT$1.2M because the app holds no total-living-cost figure. False for 2025: the captain's separate Coast FIRE planning workbook copies the app's 2025 annual total, verbatim, into a column headed "Life spend from earnings" (ratio 1.0000 against the app, verified). By her own construction the app total for 2025 IS her life-spend measure, and 2025's app total does hold Mortgage, Insurance, Rent and Tax. The claim survives only for 2023-2024, where those categories are absent from the record. This makes the coverage story cleaner, not muddier — the measure is sound at the 2025 end and incomplete exactly where the missing categories sit.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT ANSWERS HER QUESTION, done this cycle, read-only against production, every figure a ratio or share, no amount recorded anywhere:

Her premise confirmed: app 2025 / app 2023 = 2.046, matching her "roughly double" exactly, and it is app-derived (her planning workbook's 2025 figure matches the app at ratio 1.0000, so she was not reading the workbook's formula-buggy totals row). App 2024 / app 2023 = 0.950 on a ten-month record.

The gap, decomposed, additive and closing exactly at 100%:
- 11 categories absent from both earlier years: 103.2% of the gap
- shared categories, the other payer (wei): 38.8%
- like-for-like, same payer, same 14 categories: -42.0%

Like-for-like ratio, ijac only, shared categories only: 0.561. Spending on the same things, by the same person, FELL 44% between 2023 and 2025. Coverage more than fully explains the apparent doubling.

Inside the 11-category term, by share of the total gap: Mortgage 31.2%, Babies 30.3%, Entertainment 12.0%, Digital 10.1%, Insurance 6.7%, Gifts 5.7%, Transportation 5.2%, remainder under 2% combined.

Mortgage, Insurance, Rent, Tax and Tenant are self-evident coverage effects — costs she was already paying and not recording, confirmed by her own monthly mortgage schedule (complete and readable for 2022-2024, both service accounts). Babies at 30.3% is NOT self-evident: Tuition is a separate category present in all three years, so Babies is genuinely new, and whether these costs existed under another heading in 2023 is a captain question the data cannot answer.

Sizing the single largest lever: importing 2023's twelve mortgage payments alone moves the ratio 2.046 to 1.495, closing 35.2% of the gap.

WHERE THE ARCHIVE IS STILL REQUIRED, unchanged from prior cycle: what NT$1.2M actually counted (the archive workbook's other tabs, reachable via staging); anything before 2023 (2022 is entity 062; 2006-2021 blocked on credentials no working account currently holds); four October 2023 rows recorded only as a month figure in 061 Finding 6, absent from the app entirely.

GLIDE-PATH REFERENCE CHANGED: not the archive workbook's 2024-2041 projection table (dropped), but the captain's current Coast FIRE Annual tab (2025-2080, per-year Life-spend columns, both credentials read it, first data row is 2025 so it cannot answer the past but is the right forward reference).

DELIVERY CONSTRAINT, restated with its reason, unchanged: this repository is public and the report is nothing but real figures. Delivered privately; entity records only its location. Verified this cycle: every figure in the body is a ratio or a percentage share; no amount appears anywhere in the entity, a commit message, or the repo.

CHECKLIST ACCOUNTING across both ideation cycles: 4 done, 0 skipped, 0 failed on cycle 2's original checklist; the addenda (premise verification, Trap 3 measurement and reversal) were captain-directed corrections made in place with the gate withdrawn, so no fresh checklist applies to them — each is cited above with its own evidence.
